title: The community workshop
paragraphs: A small {company} offered our club a new {location} for a workshop. It was an old {garage}. We waited {outside} because the room was still {full} of boxes.
First, we had to {tidy up}. Two volunteers agreed to {take the rubbish out}. Others would {sweep the floor}, {clean the windows} and finally {clean the floor} with warm water.
My jobs were to {dust the furniture} and {vacuum the carpet}. The costume team needed to {do the washing} and {do the ironing}. Before the opening, someone also had to {do the shopping}.
We decided to {make lunch} for the helpers and {make dinner} for the evening group. Everyone promised to {do the washing up}. My {suggestion} was to {lay the table} before the visitors arrived.
I used my {phone} to {confirm} the opening time. Our leader was {positive} about the project. We wanted to {save} energy and care for the {environment} while making useful things.

title: A room for the radio club
paragraphs: Our radio club recorded a play in a pretend {living room}. An actor sat on a {sofa}, while I moved an {armchair} away from the {radiator}. We put the microphone on a low {table}.
A bright {lamp} helped us read our lines. We covered the {mirror} and closed the {curtains}. A thick {carpet} and a small {rug} made our footsteps quieter.
On the back {wall}, we hung a new {poster}. A painted {picture} stood on a narrow {shelf}. The other {shelves} held our scripts and sound equipment.
A {wardrobe} held the costumes. We borrowed a {chest of drawers} for the set. A broken {TV}, a {games console} and some {dice} became props for the actors.
The set was made from reused {wood}. Its most {unusual} {feature} was a door that opened into a painted forest. What would the finished room {look like}? We hoped our play might win a {prize}.

title: The school film team
paragraphs: Our film team visited a {historical} museum. An old {jail} appeared in a short film there. In my {opinion}, the best scene showed a {traditional} festival. We wanted to {find out} how the director made it.
The guide gave us a {clue} about the sound effects: many were recorded in the main {hall}. Some came from a {garden}, and the water sounds came from a {lake}. We {even} recorded our own footsteps.
Back at school, we filmed a scene in the {attic}, then moved a {fridge} into the studio {kitchen}. A broken {cooker} became a robot prop. The cables were stored in the {basement}.

Next, we recorded a {washing machine} in action. A {microwave} made the timer sound for our film. We put a microphone in a {cupboard}, filmed water in the {sink} and kept noisy plates out of the {dishwasher}.
For the {bathroom} scene, the camera faced the {toilet}, not the {bath}. Steam from the {shower} looked like fog. Our final scene was about sharing {housework}.

title: The home podcast challenge
paragraphs: Our class made a podcast about daily routines. In the {bedroom}, I sat on the {bed} and explained how to {make the bed}. In the {dining room}, my partner switched on the {light} and recorded the next part.
We discussed how to {reduce} waste and protect the {environment}. One idea was to {save} water when we {clean the windows}. Another was to dry clothes {outside} on sunny days.
Each speaker offered a {suggestion}. We gave our {opinion} on an {unusual} idea: a whole day without screens. The most useful {feature} of our discussion was that everyone stayed {positive}.
In the {kitchen}, we checked the {fridge} before deciding what to cook. We used the {microwave} to {make lunch}. A younger pupil showed us how to {lay the table} safely.
For our last recording, we planned to {do the shopping}, {tidy up} and {take the rubbish out}. I used a {phone} to {confirm} that every speaker was ready. Then we pressed record.
